subject: general
question: During the rule of which of the following Mughal rulers did Sunnis and Shias meet in one mosque and Christians and Jews in one church to pray, thus following the principle of 'universal peace' (sulh-i kul)?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Akbar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Akbar**, the third Mughal emperor, was known for his policy of religious tolerance and the concept of **'Sulh-i Kul'**, which translates to **'Universal Peace'**.
 
• He implemented **Sulh-i Kul** as a way to promote harmony among different religious communities, including **Sunnis, Shias, Hindus, Christians, and Jews**.
 
• Under Akbar's reign, people of different faiths often prayed together in a single mosque or church, showcasing his commitment to the principle of **religious pluralism**.
 
• Akbar established the **Ibadat Khana** (House of Worship) at Fatehpur Sikri, where he invited scholars and religious leaders from various faiths to engage in discussions and debates.
 
• He abolished the **Jizya tax**, which was levied on non-Muslims, as part of his inclusive policies.
 
• Akbar’s reign marked a significant shift in the Mughal empire's approach to governance, emphasizing **secularism and cultural integration**.
 
• His efforts to unify diverse communities under the Mughal empire were instrumental in maintaining political stability and fostering cultural growth during his rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jahangir**__

 __
 
• **Jahangir**, Akbar’s son, was known more for his patronage of the arts and architecture than for religious tolerance or innovative governance policies.
 
• His reign was marked by the consolidation of Mughal rule and artistic achievements like the construction of the **Shalimar Gardens** in Kashmir.
 
• While he continued Akbar's policies, he did not introduce any significant religious reforms akin to **Sulh-i Kul**.
 
 
 
• **Babar**__
 __
 
• **Babar**, the founder of the Mughal dynasty, was primarily focused on establishing his empire in India rather than promoting religious tolerance.
 
• Babar’s achievements include the victory at the **First Battle of Panipat** and laying the foundation of Mughal rule in India.
 
 
 
• **Humayun**__
 
 
• **Humayun**, the second Mughal emperor, faced significant challenges during his reign, including exile and the loss of his kingdom to Sher Shah Suri.
 
• His contributions were more focused on reclaiming his throne and stabilizing the empire than on religious reforms or tolerance.
